reading:
Night Timetable is the one lineage still below the yardstick. Night Departures scored 7.56, which is 0.09 under Desk Terminal, Joined. It carried on because of its best idea: the Next up tube became a departure board of the family's own next plans on lit dotted leaders. Style and the skeptic called it the best graft of heat a, and soul called it "the most convincing 1980s green screen in the heat" (8.5).

WHAT THE JUDGES LOVE, and would keep:
- The departure board.
- Vera's line down the middle of Home: the question as the first lit stop, the ways to start as stops, and the lit "Continue with Vera" terminus.
- The green-glass ask box and its pool.
- The meridian chat, with only the newest stop and its time lit.
- Setup folded to one next step.
- The Plans head sentence ("1 plan in September · next up tomorrow at 10:00"), and links that say what they open ("All 12 ideas").
- The lit NOW rule on To do.
- Archivo in three widths, with VT323 only on the glass (type: "the most coherent pairing idea in the tour").
- From the lineage's own refinement, Timetable Relit, three things the judges asked to carry into this design: Status as a lit spend board beside a printed 30-day register (style: "the best Status in the lineage"), Ideas as a one-line table, and To do in one-line rows with a labelled Edit.

WHAT SANK IT, in order of how many lenses said so:
1. Numbers in the chrome. "1 Vera 2 Ideas" in the bar and the phone tab bar reads as counts, and Home's section discs run 3, 5, 4, 2 down the page (feedback, soul, system, interaction, usability, skeptic). Lessons retired numerals in navigation for the whole tour.
2. A warm triad. Wayfinding-yellow links (even the kids' names), copper family names and initials, and amber "was due" sit side by side, so late has to fight for its colour (feedback, soul, system, style, type, usability, skeptic).
3. To do rows three lines tall, with "No active reminder" and an "Edit, complete, or snooze" disclosure on every row (feedback, system, interaction, type, usability, skeptic).
4. The board outshines the question in the squint (interaction, soul).
5. Ideas, Status and the Plans month are barely changed: card rows, default trays, an empty grid (system, skeptic, style).
6. Board rows at about 13px with no date, which wrap ("Mount St. / Helens" in the motion frame) (system, usability, type).
7. A 2.25rem amber "3" beside "Finish setting up" is the loudest mark on Home (soul).

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT WIN. Lessons say a refinement that only cleans "looks like its parent at thumbnail size". Grafts took when they drew data the page already holds and replaced something. So the winner must:
- fix all seven faults;
- give each weak page a new drawing in the lineage's own dialect (departures on leaders, lamps at stops, enamel line signs, a line only where there is order);
- bring the phosphor kit back at full, on the short list of live things only;
- make the question the largest and brightest head on Home.

On the title: "What's next for us?" was liked beside the board by soul, style and system. But usability, the skeptic and the lessons say "next" doubles the NEXT UP legend and leaves out ideas and wishes. The lessons point this lineage at the untried "What's our plan?".

briefs.name: Departures, Posted
briefs.hypothesis:
Night Departures lost 0.09 to the yardstick on faults that many lenses named, not on its idea. Six lenses marked down the numbers in the bar. Seven marked down the warm triad of yellow links, copper names and amber late. Six marked down the three-line To do rows. Two said the board beats the question in the squint. The skeptic, system and style said Ideas, Status and the month are barely changed.

This refinement fixes every one of those faults. It also brings back the three pages the judges asked to carry over from the lineage's own Timetable Relit: the Status board and register, the Ideas table and the one-line To do rows.

To avoid the "refinement only cleans" trap, every page gets a visible change in the lineage's dialect:
- The same timetable row everywhere: what, a dotted leader, the fact.
- An enamel roundel for each line in place of the numbers.
- Home's lists and board swapped either side of her line, so the lit box is met first.
- Status opening on its lit board and printed register.
- Settings as a station directory.
- The month's plans set as mini departures.

The structure the judges love stays: her line, the board, the meridian and the NOW rule. The first-read faults go.
briefs.brief:
Start from t1-timetable-graft's files: the palette json, sheet.css and templates. Keep: - her line down Home's middle (her screen, then the box as the stop you are at, then the ways to start as stops, then her last line, then the lit "Continue with Vera" terminus); - the departure board; - the meridian chat with only the newest stop lit; - the one-step service notice; - the Plans head sentence; - the To do timetable with its lit NOW rule; - Archivo in three widths (wide for names and the question, condensed for labels and figures, normal for reading), with VT323 only on the glass; - glow, screenGlow and topGlow at 1.0. 1. NO NUMBERS IN THE CHROME - base.html: take the line numerals out of `.places` and the phone tabs, and delete the `badge()` macro and its calls on Home. - The bar reads Home, Vera, Ideas, Plans, To do, Wishes (icon and word; Home comes back as usability credited on Relit), then Memory, Family, Status, Settings. - Draw "here" one way on every surface: the bar, the phone tabs, the Ideas and Plans tabs, To do's Show keys and the settings side list. - A latched cell: `background: var(--surface-3)`, with the kit's 5% white top highlight (E8). - The word in ink at weight 600. - A 2px cap along its foot in the current line's enamel (`--line-c`; steel on Home, Status and Settings). On the phone tab bar the cap goes on the top edge. - A 6px lit lamp at its top-right corner (`--lamp-fill`, `--lamp`, breathing 3.2s): the stop you are at. 2. THE LINE'S ROUNDEL IN PLACE OF ITS NUMBER - `page_head` in _ui.html: the numbered disc becomes a 2.75rem ring, 2px in the line's enamel, holding the page's pictogram in the same enamel. Ideas is lilac, Plans sky, To do teal, Wishes pink. Status, Settings, Family, Memory and the settings pages use steel. - Home's four section signs get the same ring at 1.75rem: Coming up (calendar, sky), To do (list-check, teal), Lately added (bulb, lilac), The kids' wishes (gift, pink). - One enamel lead everywhere (type: pick one length): a 3rem, 2px enamel lead at the start of the steel hairline under each head. It replaces both the 13rem page lead and the 140px section underlines. - There is no bar-foot colour strip. Enamel appears only in rings, leads, the here cap and the kind rings. 3. ONE LINK COLOUR, NO WARM TRIAD - Wayfinding yellow goes. - Links take a sheet variable `--link: #a3b9d6` (steel-denim). Underline them 1px at a .18em offset in `color-mix(in srgb,var(--link) 55%,transparent)`; on hover the underline goes to 2px and the text to ink. Links are always in sentence case. - Leave the palette's `accent` token apart from Plans' sky (the check measures the two against each other). - Copper leaves the family: - In lists, owners are ink-2 after the person icon. - In Chat, names are ink at weight 600. Initials are bone #d6ccb6 on a #1f292e disc with a 1.5px steel ring. - The family bubble's copper edge becomes a 2px steel-denim inset on the line side. - The people token survives only as the restaurant kind's clay ring. - Amber #f0b04f means late or needs a look, in words, rings and edges only. It is never a fill. - The kids' wishes: each kid is a 44px row link. The name is ink 600, then a dotted leader, then "0 open" in tabular ink-2, then a chevron. No kid's name is a yellow link any more. 4. HOME: THE BOX FIRST IN THE SQUINT This answers interaction (put the board "to the right of the question"), soul and type. - At 64rem and wider: - `grid-template-columns: minmax(18rem,1fr) minmax(26rem,1.3fr) minmax(20rem,1.05fr)`, areas `"lists line board"`. - Left column: To do, then Lately added with its "+ Add an idea" row and the "Something to eat" row. - Middle: her line. - Right: Coming up's board, with The kids' wishes under it. - Source order is her line, then the notice, then Coming up, To do, Lately added and the wishes. So the box is the first stop after the bar, and the phone follows the same order. - Rows are at `--t-item` (1.0625rem) weight 500, facts at `--t-small`. Check that "Book the campsite at Silver Falls" does not wrap at 1280. - The question, written once in _ask.html: `

`. - Archivo 110% width, 600, at 2.5rem: the largest head on Home. - "plan" takes E1's two-layer halo. - On a phone: `clamp(2rem,1.4rem + 3vw,2.5rem)`, on one line. - The box's stop ring sits on her line outside the box's left border; the skeptic saw it overlap the border on the phone. It is steel at rest and becomes a lit lamp on `.ask:focus-within`. - The box: keep `.ask-pool` (E7: phosphor from the lower-left through the kit's 2.8% scanlines) at full, a resting border at a 38% brand mix, and E4 on focus. - Send is exact #6dff9c with E3's 1px ring and 8px pool. Soul saw it render pale mint, so check `.send` is not on `--brand-hover`. - Her speaker line: her screen at 2.25rem, "Vera" at 600, then the date in condensed `--t-label`, in sentence case ("Wednesday 30 September"), not tracked capitals. - The service notice: a #131a1d plate with a 3px amber left edge. The head reads "Finish setting up", then "3 steps left" at `--t-label` 600 in amber (replacing the 2.25rem figure). Then the first step as an underlined ink link, and a "See all" disclosure at the right, so the count is said once. - The terminus: "Continue with Vera" in `--link` beside the lit terminus lamp (E20). - The board: - `align-self:start`, sized to its words, with the empty band under the time closed. - The NEXT UP inverse legend. The title bright in VT323 at 1.75rem. "10:00 Thu 1 Oct [TOMORROW]" on one line. - The radar at 6.5rem in its own top-right corner beside that block, at full E17 light (sweep, hub, blips), never behind text (style's fix 1). - A dim rule, then three departure rows in VT323 at 1.3rem, which reads at about 15px (system, usability). Each row is `grid-template-columns: 7ch 5ch minmax(0,1fr) auto`: - the day, "Sun 4 Oct", dim; - the time, "13:00", bright; - the destination link on one line, cut with an ellipsis, the full title in its `title` attribute, with a dot leader filling the rest; - "in 4 days", dim, at the right. - No row ever wraps. Then "› 1 more" and the cursor. - The calendar note sits under the case at `--t-small`. - Home's To do: a 44px tick on its stop, the title, then one meta line ("Alex · was due 3 days ago", the late words in amber). - Lately added: one-line rows. The kind pictogram in a 1.5rem kind ring, the name at 500, a leader, and the kind word in label ink. - The row afterglow, which the harness's motion-glow frames capture on the first `.idea-card`: pointing at a row lights a 2px phosphor edge on its left and its kind ring. Both light at `--glow-in` and fade over `--afterglow`, which is T1-33's visible afterglow, not a steel wash. 5. ONE ROW DRAWING: THE DEPARTURE Every list row is what (ink 500), then a dotted leader, then the fact in tabular condensed Archivo at the right. - The leader: steel at 35%, 1px dots every 5px, drawn only where a fact follows, capped at 46rem. - It is used on Home's lists, the board, Ideas, Status and Settings. 6. TO DO (tasks.html) This is six lenses' fault. Bring Relit's rows from tour/t1-a/variants/t1-timetable-refine/templates/tasks.html (around lines 88-131) and their rules in that sheet. At 52rem and wider, each task is one line: - A margin stamp in two lines (T1-14's pairing): "Sun 27 Sep" over "19:56", condensed and tabular, amber when late; "No date" in faint. - The line with its stop: filled amber when late, a steel ring for what is to come, and the lit NOW lamp and rule between the two (kept). - A 44px tick. - A faint "#4", then the title. - Who: the person icon and the name in ink-2. - The due words at the right: "was due 3 days ago" in amber, "due tomorrow" in ink-2. - A ghost Edit key (pencil and "Edit", 44px). Its form opens across the whole row (L204). Also: - Delete "No active reminder" from every row. Show the bell and time only when a reminder is set. Notes, window and repeats go on a second line only when they exist. - Head lede: "4 open · 2 late", with "2 late" in amber. Remove the "4 shown" line. - "Add something to do" stays the one primary. 7. IDEAS (ideas.html) Bring Relit's table from t1-timetable-refine/templates/ideas.html: - Column heads: #, Kind, Idea, For, By road, Way. Direction gets its own 3ch column (type's fix 4). - One line per idea. The kind is its ring plus the word in label ink. For is in ink-2. The drive time is right-aligned and tabular, like a departure time. - Lede: "12 ideas · 10 on the radar". - The portrait radar: capped at 20rem tall, sticky, with its reading note under the case (L268), not on the glass. - The filters on one row at 64rem and wider. 8. PLANS (plans_month.html, plans.html) - Head lede counting what is shown (T1-34's caveat): "1 in September, 2 in early October · next up tomorrow at 10:00". - The calendar note moves under the head (style). - Rows are as tall as their content: 3rem for an empty week, from 6rem for a week holding a plan or today. - Days gone by: numerals faint. Days outside the month: sunk to #0a0d0c. - Today: a steel ring, a lit lamp and "Today" at `--t-label`. - Each plan in a cell is a mini departure on one line: "17:00" in condensed 600 tabular, then the destination with an ellipsis, on slate with a 2px sky edge. - The List view becomes a printed timetable: day | time | destination on a leader | in N days | the kind as the platform word. 9. STATUS (write status.html) Style, system and the skeptic: "still the default trays". - Lede: "6 working · about $0.00 of $2.00 spent today". - The first band, above the fold, is T1-37 from t1-timetable-refine/templates/status.html (lines 74-117) and that sheet's .spend-month and .spend-figure rules: - the spend tube at full E12-E15 light; - beside it, the printed register: "The last 30 days, about", then "$1.26", then "over 6 model calls"; - the cache sentence, and "Change the limit". - Below it, Who answers, Keys and Connected to as three timetable plates, one line per row: the lamp (lit when on; a steel ring when off; red only when something has stopped), then the name, then the detail in ink-2 on a leader. - Who answers draws its order as a short steel line down its lamps, ending at the fallback's ring. 10. SETTINGS (settings.html) A station directory in place of nine cards: - One plate, two columns at 64rem and wider, one 56px row link per part: its pictogram in a 1.75rem steel ring, the name at 600, a leader, the state sentence clamped to one line, and a chevron. - Sign-in and security gets a 3px amber edge, an amber ring and "Needs a look" in amber words. - Lede: "9 parts · 1 needs a look". - The General page keeps its side list as a line with stops, the current stop lit. 11. CHAT (chat.html) - The head moves to the left edge as on every page (interaction): her screen at 2.75rem in the ring's place, then "Vera", then the lede at 60ch. - On a phone the head is one line and the lede is hidden below 40rem, so the first stop shows on the first screen. - Keep the meridian: the dateline once, the times at the line in tabular figures, the family on the right, only the newest stop lit. 12. THE FORM (idea_form.html) - The head ring in lilac. - Labels in sentence case, 600, at `--t-small`, in label ink (no tracked capitals). - Wells #0c1214 with a 1px #6d7a80 edge, and E4 on focus. - "Add it" is the one lit primary. The crumb is in `--link`. 13. TYPE - Keep the nine named steps. - Ledes at max 60ch with `text-wrap: pretty`. - Every time and count in tabular figures. - Capitals only on the glass legends and column heads, at .06em or less. 14. THE LIGHT At the kit's full strength, and only on this list: - the mark and its cursor (E2); - "plan" (E1); - the box's pool and its focus (E7, E4); - Send (E3); - the focus ring (E5); - the top haze (E6); - the board, the Ideas radar and the spend tube (E12-E17, with the 0.35px blur on the glass); - the lamps (E20): here, the box's stop while typing, the terminus, NOW, Status, today; - her screen (E19); - the newest chat stop; - the row afterglow (E9) and the landing flash (E10); - sign in and the 404 (E16, E22). Keep the kit's reduced-motion, more-contrast and forced-colours blocks. Every target is 44px.
briefs.borrows:
The judges' fixes, most-cited first:
1. Numerals out of the bar, the phone tabs and Home's section discs; Home back in the bar: feedback, soul, system, interaction, usability, skeptic, and lessons' retirement of numbered chrome.
2. The warm triad resolved:
   - steel-denim underlined links: feedback, soul, system, skeptic;
   - owner names in ink-2: type, usability, style;
   - kids' names in ink, not links: style, system;
   - bone or steel for the chat's family, not copper: feedback, skeptic.
3. To do in one-line rows, with "No active reminder" and the disclosure gone and a labelled Edit: feedback, system, interaction ("use refine's one-line rows"), type, usability, skeptic.
4. The question beats the board. The board goes to the right of the question: interaction. The box and Send get the strongest light: interaction and soul (Send exact #6dff9c). The board is sized to content, with the radar given its own corner: style's fix 1.
5. Ideas as Relit's one-line table: system, skeptic, style. Direction in its own column: type's fix 4 on Relit.
6. Status: Relit's board and register (T1-37, style: "carry it into the graft") at the top, with a figure in the head: skeptic, system.
7. Board rows at about 15px with their dates, never wrapping: system, usability, type (keep the day with its time).
8. The amber "3" at label size: soul.
9. Plans: the note under the head and plans as mini departures (style); weeks sized to content (skeptic's "fold empty weeks", done here by height); lede counts what is shown (T1-34's caveat from feedback, usability, skeptic).
10. Chat's head at the left edge: interaction. A phone head that lets the thread start on the first screen: the designer's own weakness.
11. Ledes at 60ch and one length of enamel lead: type on Relit.
12. The box's stop ring outside the box on the phone: skeptic.

Small borrowings, each answering a fault:
- Relit's own pages, from tour/t1-a/variants/t1-timetable-refine/templates/tasks.html, ideas.html and status.html and that folder's sheet.css.
- T1-14, two-line due stamps, from tour/t1-b/variants/t1-console-refine/templates/tasks.html (lines 145-160).
- L204, the edit form opening across the row, from Quote Board at Evening.
- L268, the reading note under the case, from Track Diagram Relit.
- T1-33's visible afterglow as a phosphor edge (lessons: "give it a phosphor edge and a second place to show").
- A lamp on the current key, after L140 (a strong "here", among the universal fixes).

Phosphor: the kit's E1-E22 at full, on the list in section 14.
briefs.title: What’s our *plan*? This improves on both of the lineage's titles. It keeps the household voice the judges liked in "What's next for us?" ("our" for "us"). It lights "plan", the job word that won 13 of 16 title notes. It drops "next", which usability, the skeptic and the lessons said doubles the NEXT UP board beside it and leaves out ideas and wishes. It is the lessons' own untried suggestion for this lineage. At 16 characters it holds one line at 2.5rem on a phone, and the board beside it answers the question with the family's own departures.

briefs.name: Night Interchange
briefs.hypothesis:
Grafts that took in round 1 drew data the page already holds and replaced something the page did badly. This brief takes four features and rebuilds each as a piece of the station:
- The ways to start become interchanges with the Plans, To do and Ideas lines. Her line then shows, before you press, where Vera will put what you say, and Home's centre gains grounded colour with a job.
- The departure board refreshes as Home opens: a line of light runs down the glass and the departures come up behind it. That is the original tube's warm-up with a job, and the harness's motion-on frames capture it.
- Departed weeks fold away on the Plans month, so the page every heat-a lineage but Pocket left as an empty grid now gives its height to the weeks to come.
- Status becomes a service-status board whose state is said in words, which interaction called "the clearest state language in the heat".

Three of the four are gems from lower-half designs. It also applies the lineage's most-cited fixes: no numbers, one link colour, one-line To do rows, the Ideas table. It should beat the carried design on the pages the judges called unchanged, and give the tournament a second answer to Home. The board stays left but is joined to her line by what the interchanges promise; the refinement puts the board on the right instead.
briefs.brief:
Start from t1-timetable-graft's files. Keep Home's arrangement: the board and the kids' wishes on the left, her line in the middle, To do and Lately added on the right. Keep the meridian chat, the one-step notice, the To do NOW rule, Archivo in widths with VT323 on the glass, and glow 1.0 across the board. A. THE LINEAGE'S FIXES FIRST - Numbers out of the chrome: - base.html: no numerals in `.places` or the phone tabs. The bar reads Home, Vera, Ideas, Plans, To do, Wishes. - Delete the `badge()` discs on Home. - Each section sign leads with its line's pictogram in its enamel, at 1.25rem with no disc. - Page heads replace the numbered disc with the pictogram in a 2.75rem slate tile (#1f292e) carrying a 2px enamel cap on its top edge. - Keep the carried enamel lead under each sign, at one length (3rem) everywhere. Drop the bar-foot strip. - "Here" is a latched surface-3 cell with the enamel cap and a 6px lit lamp (E20) in its corner. - Links: `--link: #a3b9d6`, underlined, in sentence case. Yellow is gone. - Owners and family names in ink-2 or ink, never copper. Kids' names are ink rows with "0 open" on a leader. The chat's family bubble takes a 2px steel-denim edge. Amber means late or needs a look only. - Send is exact #6dff9c with E3's ring and pool. - "Finish setting up" with "3 steps left" at the label step in amber, and "See all" as the disclosure. - The board: - `align-self:start`, the empty glass under the time closed, the radar at 6.5rem in a clear top-right corner at full E17 light. - Rows in VT323 at 1.3rem on a `7ch 5ch minmax(0,1fr) auto` grid: "Sun 4 Oct" dim | "13:00" bright | the destination on one line with an ellipsis | "in 4 days". Never wrapping. - The question inside the box's frame, at 2.5rem Archivo wide 600 (the largest head), with its stop ring on her line outside the box. - To do (tasks.html): one line per task. Carry Relit's rows from tour/t1-a/variants/t1-timetable-refine/templates/tasks.html: - the margin "Sun 27 Sep" over "19:56", amber when late; - the line with an amber stop for late and a steel ring for what is to come, with the lit NOW rule between; - the tick, "#4", the title, who in ink-2, the due words at the right; - an "Edit" key whose form opens across the row; - no "No active reminder"; - the lede "4 open · 2 late". - Ideas (ideas.html): Relit's one-line table (#, Kind, Idea, For, By road, Way) beside the capped portrait radar. Lede "12 ideas · 10 on the radar". - Chat: the head at the left edge, one line on a phone. B. FEATURE 1, INTERCHANGES ON HER LINE (L052, a gem), in _ask.html and the sheet - Each way to start is keyed to the line its message lands on. Key it by what the starter says, not by its position: - `{% set to = 'todo' if starter.say.startswith('Remind') else ('ideas' if starter.say.startswith('We should') else 'plans') %}
  • `. - The sheet already maps `.to-plans`, `.to-todo` and `.to-ideas` to `--c`. - Each starter's stop on her line becomes an interchange: - a 16px ring, 2px steel, with a 6px core disc in `--c`; - the 12px stub from her line to the key drawn in `--c`, so her line visibly branches to the Plans, To do and Ideas lines; - the key: a slate plate at least 44px tall, with a 3px `--c` cap on its left edge (L052's 8px tab, thinned as its caveat asks), the words in ink; - at the key's right end, the destination line's pictogram (calendar, list-check or bulb) at 1rem in `--c`, `aria-hidden`, since the words already say it. - Pointing at or focusing a key lights its interchange core as a phosphor lamp at `--glow-in`, fading over `--afterglow` (E9): the stop you are about to take. - The same drawing on the empty chat's starters. - The terminus stays the one lit ring, and "Continue with Vera" goes in `--link`. C. FEATURE 2, THE BOARD REFRESHES (L110, a gem), in home.html and the sheet - Add `` inside the board's tube, after the rows. - The sweep: `position:absolute; left:.9rem; right:.9rem; height:2px; z-index:5`, with a `linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, color-mix(in srgb,var(--screen) 60%,#fff) 20% 80%, transparent)` core. Box shadow: a 14px bloom, `0 0 14px 3px` at 40% screen, and an 18px trailing wash above, `0 -18px 24px -6px` at 12%. - It runs once: `animation: board-sweep 1.25s cubic-bezier(.45,0,.55,1) .15s 1 both`. The keyframes go from `top:.7rem; opacity:0`, to opacity 1 at 8% and 0.7 at 80%, to `top:calc(100% - 1.7rem); opacity:0`. - The NEXT UP block powers on from a line first (E16, starting at `opacity:.05`). - Each `.board-rows li` comes up as the line passes it: - `animation: dep-in .45s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.3,1) both`; - delays of .35s, .6s and .85s through `:nth-child(1..3)` rules (no inline style); - `dep-in` starts at `opacity:.05`, with the time flashing hot (`color:#dcffe8`, a 10px halo), and settles to its normal strength. - It never loops and never runs on hover. The harness's motion-on frames (60, 220, 450 and 900ms) will show the line crossing and the departures arriving. - Reduced motion: no sweep, and the rows are simply there. More contrast: the sweep is hidden. D. FEATURE 3, DEPARTED WEEKS FOLD AWAY (L125, a gem), in plans_month.html and the sheet - A week whose last day is before today is a departed service: `{% set departed = week[-1].date < t0 %}`. - A departed row: - folds to a 2.75rem strip on green-black (`color-mix(in srgb,var(--bg) 85%,var(--surface))`), stepping back into the dark; - day numerals in faint at weight 400; - its plans as inline mini departures, "17:00 Pho Oregon", in dim ink at `--t-small`, each padded to a 44px hit area. - This week never folds. Today gets a steel ring, a lit lamp and "Today". - Weeks to come stay tall, from 6rem. Each plan there is a one-line mini departure: "13:00" in condensed 600 tabular, then the destination with an ellipsis (the full title in its `title` attribute), on slate with a 2px sky edge. - Days outside the month are sunk (#0a0d0c). - The head lede counts what is shown: "1 in September, 2 in early October · next up tomorrow at 10:00". - The calendar note goes under the head. - The phone's list shows only the busy days, the departed ones dimmed. E. FEATURE 4, SERVICE STATUS IN WORDS (T1-13), in status.html (write it; the carried design used today's) - Lede: "6 working · about $0.00 of $2.00 spent today". - Then one plate, "Service status", with Who answers, Keys and Connected to as three column groups.
